report:
Reviewed the complete syntax_identities claim, four ordinary implementation associations and both test entries. parse/mod.rs creates a temporary tree-sitter Tree, walks children in source order into Vec<LocalModItemSym>, converts malformed nodes (has_error), unsupported children, unsupported non-macro expressions and dangling attributes to explicit Error spans, and never publishes the parser tree. Its cfg filtering is intentional conditional inclusion; comments and delimiters are not definitions. parse/items.rs constructs owned Stashed CST data and name/scope/span identities for functions, structs, enums, traits, impls, aliases, constants, statics, uses and macro forms. Relative CST offsets and the captured absolute_span helper preserve placement and ParseSource provenance; inline modules create their own scope and specify their children, while file-backed modules retain the selected source. local_syms/mods.rs unexpanded_items explicitly uses ScopeSymbol::Module(module) for file-backed bodies, preserving ownership. local_syms/structs.rs demonstrates the identity/detail split: name and scope are identity fields while CST and span are tracked detail, and checking/resolution occurs in the separately requested sig/fields operations. Parser item constructors allocate syntax, not checked semantic results. Macro definitions retain owned token syntax; modules retain body source and ordered child-query output instead of a tree-sitter node. Added essential associations for these three additional implementation files so their changes invalidate this review.

The ordinary items_in_a_file_backed_module_use_that_module_as_their_scope test registers lib.rs and child.rs, finds the child module and its Holder struct, and directly asserts Holder.scope == Module(child). Captured helpers show actual source-file registration, tracked root creation, parsing and query specification; there is no hidden assertion substitute. This test detects ownership accidentally assigned to the root module. Executed cargo test -p sage-test-harness --lib items_in_a_file_backed_module_use_that_module_as_their_scope: one passed, zero failed.

The explicit todo::modules_parse_syntax_identities remains deferred and is not counted as a behavioral test. Its comment specifies the missing source/generated-fixture matrix for ordering, ownership, CST and provenance, malformed/unsupported inputs and a parse-only query trace excluding resolution/signature/body/solver work. Completing that fixture matrix and isolating the parse-only trace are its prerequisites. Stable identity across edits and absence of published parser representation are supported by source structure here, not claimed as exercised by the existing ownership assertion. Full dynamic validation of these dimensions remains within that honest TODO; accepting it does not claim complete test implementation. No N/A entries exist. Source inspection found no contradictory implementation in the reviewed parsing and publication paths. cargo fmt completed; broader build and centralized post-codegen/sanity checks are coordinated separately.
